review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the qExpand simp lemmas in Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_X0.lean, the repeated algebraMap-to-single/C lemmas in other Definitions files, and the relevant HahnSeries simp attributes in Mathlib. The file has no simp attributes of its own. The findings below are about missing simp-facing lemmas, where the same `algebraMap`/`HahnSeries.C` bridge is rewritten by hand. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about how simp would behave. The main uncertainty is whether a global simp attribute on `algebraMap_eq_C` would clash with other files' `algebraMap` normal forms, because the project has several other algebraMap-to-single/C lemmas. A scoped or local simp set avoids that risk.

findings.declaration: ModularCurve.W1.algebraMap_eq_C / qTwist_C (algebraMap vs HahnSeries.C normal form)
findings.excerpt: theorem algebraMap_eq_C (c : K) : algebraMap K (LaurentSeries K) c = HahnSeries.C c := by
findings.problem: The scalar embedding `algebraMap K (LaurentSeries K) c` and `HahnSeries.C c` are two forms of the same term. The library's simp lemma `qExpand_C` and the file's `qTwist_C` only fire on the `HahnSeries.C` form. `qTwist_single` fires on `single` and does not help here. No lemma tagged simp (or otherwise canonical) converts the algebraMap form to the C form. So every user must do an explicit `rw [algebraMap_eq_C, qExpand_C]` or `rw [algebraMap_eq_C, qTwist_C]`. This happens at lines 61, 85, 91, 245 and 259. Line 259 even rewrites `algebraMap_eq_C, qExpand_C, ← algebraMap_eq_C` to go there and back, which shows the missing canonical form. The lemma `qTwist_C` is also not simp, although its sibling `qExpand_C` is.
findings.proposed_change: Choose HahnSeries.C as the canonical form and tag `algebraMap_eq_C` with `@[simp]`, or put it in a local simp set. Tag `qTwist_C` with `@[simp]` to match `qExpand_C`. Better still, add `qExpand_algebraMap` and `qTwist_algebraMap`, each stating that the map fixes `algebraMap K (LaurentSeries K) c`, and tag them simp. This removes the round trip `algebraMap_eq_C, qExpand_C, ← algebraMap_eq_C` in `hP2` and lets `simp` close the `RingHom.ext` obligations in `qTwist_aeval` and `qExpand_aeval`.
findings.benefit: Users get one normal form for scalar constants and one simp lemma set for twist and expand. The manual rewrite-and-reverse chains become `simp` calls. The chains also stop depending on the order of rewrites.

theorem qTwist_C (u : Kˣ) (c : K) : qTwist u (HahnSeries.C c) = HahnSeries.C c := by
algebraMap R₀ (LaurentSeries R) r = HahnSeries.C (algebraMap R₀ R r)

findings.excerpt: theorem qExpand_aeval (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (x : LaurentSeries K) (P : Polynomial K) :
findings.problem: These are the canonical push-through lemmas for `aeval`: a ring hom of Laurent series commutes with `aeval`. They carry no simp attribute. Their uses are all explicit rewrites, at lines 181, 185, 188, 248 and 258. Line 258 uses `← qExpand_aeval` and then `qExpand_aeval, qExpand_aeval` in the same rewrite chain. These rewrites are done by hand and in both directions. The file therefore has no stated simp direction and no unfolding step for `aeval` under `qTwist` and `qExpand`.
findings.proposed_change: State the orientation `qExpand K N (aeval x P) = aeval (qExpand K N x) P` as the simp direction, which pushes the ring hom to the argument. Tag it `@[simp]` after `qExpand_aeval` and `qTwist_aeval` are given the algebraMap/C constant lemmas from the previous finding. Keep `←` rewrites only where `hjp` needs them. Then `F6`, `F7` and `hP1` can be written as `simpa using congrArg (qExpand K p) hstar` or similar, instead of `rwa [map_mul, map_pow, map_one, qExpand_aeval]`.
findings.benefit: Callers get a fixed normal form where qExpand and qTwist are pushed inside `aeval`. The roughly five bespoke rewrite chains need fewer exact-order `rw` steps. The `←` uses at line 258 become unnecessary.

evidence.excerpt: rwa [map_mul, map_pow, (qExpand K p).map_one, qExpand_aeval] at h
